text:
praveen: FYI - after the kernel patch we rolled to a subset of Dedicated hosts last night, we're seeing steady KV cache memory growth for long-context traces (~4k tokens). Hosted tenants not affected. Private/onprem shows bursty eviction spikes instead of gradual growth. Anyone seen this pattern before?

sylvie: can you paste the profiler output? :mag:

praveen: quick snapshot from the canary host (A100 pool, Dedicated):
```
# top-kv-usage (truncated)
PID   KV_RSS   cache_slots  evict_count
2345  6.1G     1.2M         0
2345  6.3G     1.3M         0
2345  6.7G     1.5M         3
2345  7.1G     1.6M         6

perf record -e page-faults -p 2345 -- sleep 60
# perf script: shows page-walks inside kernel module path after kernel bump
```

andre: interesting. Hosted not affected suggests routing/kernel/config differences. Did the kernel bump also change default compaction or THP settings?

praveen: rollout note from infra-bot indicates kernel: 5.15.0+inhouse-rc (debian-variant) with a patch that touched page-cache heuristics. infra-bot:deploy: 
"deployed kernel image to pool:dedi-gpu-a100-1"

maria: On Private clusters we restrict MTU to 1400 and disable GSO/GRO for troubleshooting. Could that cause different kernel behaviour for our driver pagewalk/coalescing?

andre: It can. Smaller MTU + disabled offloads can increase CPU interrupt rate + cause more small IOs. For KV cache our evict path uses asynchronous IO for slab writeback; the backpressure can change reuse patterns.

praveen: Repro plan I ran:
```bash
# short repro (runs in container with same userland)
./tools/kv-stress --seqlen 4096 --concurrency 8 --prefix-cache 0.25 --report-interval 15
# capture memmaps and kvmalloc stats
pmap 2345 | grep kvcache
cat /proc/zoneinfo | egrep 'page.*compaction'
```
Got steady +600MB/hour growth until eviction started thrashing.

sylvie: Do we quantize kernels differently per pool? Kernel features and GCC flags can affect behavior. Also what about jemalloc arenas vs tcmalloc on Dedicated vs Hosted?

praveen: Good call — Dedicated images use jemalloc-5.3 custom build, Hosted uses tcmalloc shim + optmem. Private is mixed. I ran a quick allocator heap profile: jemalloc shows high fragmentation ratio ~1.45 in the canary.

andre: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel page reclaim patch altered async writeback ordering, increasing intervals between slab coalesces and causing more fragmentation over long contexts; 2) allocator + kernel combo (jemalloc + new kernel) surfaces a regression in slot reuse, so pages remain resident longer until a larger eviction wave occurs.

maria: For Private we also see OOM-kill tolerant policy set to conservative (vm.overcommit=0) which makes evict waves more aggressive. That explains the sporadic spikes vs steady growth.

praveen: Quick mitigation attempted: lowered kvcache_dirty_thresh from 0.6 -> 0.45 and forced more frequent background compaction on the canary. Growth rate dropped ~4x in the 2nd hour. Still want root cause.

andre: Can you capture slab histograms + page-placement traces? If this is kernel reclaim ordering, perf record -e mm:page_reclaim and ftrace on mm/reclaim should show it. Also capture /proc/spl_kv_stats (we added slab counters)

praveen: Will run those. Repro across environments: hosted container run with identical userland + same kernel does NOT reproduce (so userland alone isn't enough). Seems config & kernel build flags matter.

sylvie: Another angle — kernel cfg tweak in dedicated AMI enabled CONFIG_CGROUP_MEM_RES_CTRL or changed memory cgroup pressure handling? That affects how we measure RSS and when we trigger eviction in our runtime.

maria: Suggestion: for Dedicated pool, pin canary hosts to previous kernel image and run A/B for 24h. If rollback stops growth it's almost certainly kernel-related. I'll schedule rollback window for 03:30 UTC.

praveen: Thanks. I'll attach perf + slab dumps to the canary ticket and post links here when ready. For immediate safety I'll reduce maximum long-context length by 10% on Dedicated to limit growth exposure. :lock:

infra-bot: rollout: kernel-5.14-stable pinned to pool:dedi-gpu-a100-1 at 03:30 UTC per schedule by maria

andre: Also add a short-lived metric for kvcache_fragmentation_ratio per tenant so SRE can alert before eviction cascades. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria: Agreed. I'll create the alert (kvcache.frag > 1.25 for 10m).

praveen: OK will follow up after the A/B run. If rollback proves it, next steps: revert patch + submit smaller follow-up that isolates page-cache heuristic change.

sylvie: Thanks team — great triage. Keep notes in the ticket and drop the perf artifacts here. :thumbsup:
